result.title: Annual Meeting of the New Champions 2026
result.description:
AI, clean energy, biotech - the technologies defining the next decades are already here.

The bigger question is: can we turn them into better jobs, stronger economies and new opportunities?

That’s the focus of the World Economic Forum’s Annual Meeting of the New Champions 2026, taking place from June 23–25 in Dalian, China.

Known as “Summer Davos”, AMNC26 will bring together over 1,700 participants from business, government, science, academia and civil society under the theme Innovating at Scale.

Together, participants will take on some of the biggest questions of the moment: What’s next for trade and industry? Where is China’s economy headed? How can new technologies create real value? And how can growth generate more opportunities for the next generation? They’ll also look at how the energy transition can help drive competitiveness in a rapidly changing world.

Livestreamed sessions from the meeting will be available on the Forum’s website and YouTube channel.

Follow #AMNC26 and #2026夏季达沃斯# for updates from the ground.

result.title: Inside The Factories of the Future | WEF | Top Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:14 - A peek into the factories of the future: In this documentary, we travel to Viet Nam, Türkiye and the United States to step inside three leading manufacturing facilities recognized by the World Economic Forum's Global Lighthouse Network.

02:02 - 5 commencement speakers give advice to graduates: It’s graduation season in many countries, and luminaries from tech, academia, business and beyond are giving advice to new graduates on success and well-being. Here are 5 memorable quotes from commencement ceremonies in the US from: Jensen Huang of Nvidia, Jonathan Haidt of NYU Stern, hedge fund founder Ray Dalio, Thasunda Brown Duckett of TIAA, and former Walmart CEO Kathryn McLay.

04:06 - The energy transition is entering a new era: Energy systems are being tested by rising demand, geopolitical uncertainty and affordability pressures — making resilience, security and investment conditions central to the next phase of the transition. Here, the World Economic Forum’s Head of Energy and Materials, Roberto Bocca, shares insights from the Energy Transition Index 2026 and explains why transition pathways will differ across countries.

07:07 - Greece is turning its coal heartland into a green energy hub: Western Macedonia is one of Greece’s former industrial strongholds. It became prosperous by mining lignite - a soft brown form of #coal - which provided 70% of Greece's energy. In a post-coal age, however, the region has faced difficulties, with a decline in jobs, industries and population. Now, utility company DEH Greece, as its CEO Georgios Stassis explains, has a plan to turn the region into a powerhouse for the information era.

result.title: Half the world’s leaders should be women, says Iceland’s former PM
result.description:
Women make up half the global workforce, but hold only a third of corporate leadership roles. Iceland's former PM Katrin Jakobsdóttir argues this isn't just an equity issue — it's a missed opportunity for better decision-making, since diverse leadership teams consistently outperform homogeneous ones.

Here, Jakobsdóttir unpacks the practical barriers — from childcare and parental leave policy to board hiring practices — that keep capable people out of leadership.

result.title: What Happens Inside the World's Most Advanced Factories?
result.description:
What does the factory of the future actually look like?

In this documentary, we travel to Viet Nam, Türkiye and the United States to step inside three leading manufacturing facilities recognized by the World Economic Forum's Global Lighthouse Network.

From AI-assisted production and workforce training to renewable energy and resource efficiency, we explore how companies including Foxconn Industrial Internet (FII), @beko and @ericsson are rethinking the way factories operate.

What we found wasn't just new technology – it was people learning, adapting and helping shape the future of manufacturing.

0:00 - Welcome to the factories of the future
1:23 - Foxconn FII, Vietnam: the lights-out factory
5:22 - BEKO, Türkiye: upskilling the workforce
10:29 - Ericsson, Texas: the sustainable smart factory
14:34 - The factory of the future

To find out how over two hundred Global Lighthouses are pushing the boundaries of what’s possible and forging a path forward for industries, follow this link: https://initiatives.weforum.org/global-lighthouse-network/home

result.title: These countries are leading the energy transition in 2026
result.description:
The energy transition is underway. But progress around the world is uneven. Which countries are furthest ahead? And which are catching up the fastest?

The Energy Transition Index benchmarks the progress of 120 countries towards a more secure, equitable and sustainable energy future. Familiar names are at the top this year, but there is notable progress elsewhere, as Roberto Bocca, Head of the Forum’s Centre for Energy and Materials, explains.
